sec: GLP-1 versus GIP and complications of insulin deficiency

items.q: Match the incretin to its source — 1) GLP-1 2) GIP … A) L cells of ileum and colon B) K cells of jejunum
items.exp: The table gives GLP-1 from L cells of ileum and colon and GIP from K cells of jejunum. (Book p929)

items.q: Assess the first GLP-1 versus GIP rows: I Both have +++ glucose-dependent insulin release. II Both have +++ enhancement of beta-cell glucose responsiveness.
items.exp: Both columns show +++ for glucose-dependent insulin release and for enhancement of beta-cell glucose responsiveness. (Book p929)

items.q: Which incretin column has +++ suppression of glucagon release?
items.exp: The table shows +++ under GLP-1 and dashes under GIP for suppression of glucagon release. (Book p929)

items.q: Match the listed effect to the stronger incretin column — 1) Stimulates beta-cell expansion 2) Inhibits gastric emptying 3) Enhances satiety 4) Reduces body weight … A) GLP-1 B) GLP-1 C) GLP-1 D) GLP-1
items.exp: For each of these rows the GLP-1 column is marked +++ while GIP has dashes. (Book p929)

items.q: What half-life is written for GLP-1 in the table?
items.exp: The GLP-1 half-life row states 1–2 minutes and notes rapid degradation by DPP-4. (Book p929)

items.q: The GIP half-life in the table is written as ___ minutes.
items.exp: The GIP half-life row reads 5–7 minutes. (Book p929)

items.q: Which page-listed feature supports choosing recombinant GLP-1 over another hypoglycemic agent?
items.exp: The advantages list includes no risk of hypoglycemia, weight loss, cardio-protection, HbA1c reduction and nephroprotection. (Book p929)

items.q: The page says recombinant GLP-1 is used in treatment of which liver-fat condition?
items.exp: The advantages list says recombinant GLP-1 promotes weight loss and is used in treatment of NASH/NAFLD. (Book p929)

items.q: Assess the nephron note: I Adult diabetes is associated with nephron underdosing. II Low birth weight is linked to decreased nephron number in Bartter’s theory.
items.exp: The note links adult diabetes with nephron underdosing, low birth weight, decreased nephron number and Bartter’s theory. (Book p929)

items.q: Match the insulin-deficiency complication group to its examples — 1) Acute 2) Chronic 3) Macrovascular … A) DKA and HHS B) Retinopathy, nephropathy and peripheral neuropathy C) Atherosclerotic CVD and CKD
items.exp: The complication diagram lists DKA/HHS under acute, retinopathy/nephropathy/peripheral neuropathy under chronic, and atherosclerotic CVD/CKD under macrovascular. (Book p929)

items.q: Which is the odd one out among the acute complications listed under insulin deficiency?
items.exp: Retinopathy is in the chronic column; DKA and HHS are listed in the acute column. (Book p929)

items.q: Which precipitating factor for DKA appears in the right-hand list?
items.exp: The DKA precipitating-factor list includes cocaine and non-compliance to treatment. (Book p929)
